common.freeBuildTitle: Free build: draw any molecule or ion
common.boardHint: Drag an element onto the board, or click it to add it next to the selected atom (bonded to it). Drag from an atom's blue ring to another atom to bond them. Click a bond to change its order.

hints.start: Add atoms to the board to start.
hints.connect: Bond every atom into one structure.
hints.atomsPattern: The atoms don't match the formula. {{details}}
hints.placeRemainingPattern: Electrons still to place: {{count}}. Put them as lone pairs on the outer atoms first.
hints.tooManyPattern: Too many electrons placed ({{count}} extra): take off lone pairs or lower a bond order.
hints.shortPattern: {{atom}} has only {{count}} electrons. Turn a lone pair on a neighbour into a multiple bond.
hints.overPattern: {{atom}} has {{count}} electrons, more than it can hold.
hints.done: Every rule is met. Press Check to compare with the best structure.

selection.none: Select an atom or a bond to edit it.

feedback.incomplete: Not finished yet: work through the checklist.
feedback.wrongSkeleton: The electrons are all placed, but the atoms are joined differently from the real molecule.
feedback.best: Correct! This is the best Lewis structure.
feedback.bestResonancePattern: Correct! This is one of {{count}} equivalent resonance structures.
feedback.alternative: Correct: every atom keeps an octet. Expanding the central atom would give smaller formal charges; both answers are accepted.
feedback.acceptable: Valid, with the smallest formal charges, but the negative formal charge belongs on the more electronegative atom.
feedback.minor: A valid Lewis structure, but not the best one: another arrangement has smaller formal charges.
feedback.notBest: A valid Lewis structure, but its formal charges are much larger than they need to be.
feedback.tooLarge: This drawing is too large to check.

board.name: Drawing board
board.helpText: Arrow keys move between atoms. L adds a lone pair, D an unpaired electron, B starts a bond, G moves the atom, Delete removes it. Add atoms with the element palette.
board.empty: The board is empty. Add atoms with the element palette.

status.incompleteAllowed: Incomplete octet, allowed for this element

board.noLonePairPattern: {{atom}} has no lone pair to remove.
board.bondModePattern: Bond from {{atom}}. Choose a partner with the arrow keys, then press Enter, or 1, 2 or 3 for the bond order. Escape cancels.
board.noPartner: There is no other atom to bond to.
board.grabbedPattern: Moving {{atom}}. Arrow keys move it; Enter drops it.
board.tileHelp: Adds the atom next to the selected atom, bonded to it, or in the middle of an empty board.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area has a drawing board where you build a Lewis structure from atoms, bonds, lone pairs and unpaired electrons, with a palette of elements beside it.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has the molecule chooser, the valence-electron count, a checklist of the rules, Check and Show answer buttons, and Reset All.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Choose a molecule, add atoms from the palette, bond them, then add lone pairs until every electron is placed.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows one resonance form of the chosen molecule or ion, its hybrid, or a skeleton to complete, with a gallery of all its resonance forms.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has the molecule chooser, the view choice, buttons to step through the forms, and Reset All.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Choose an ion such as nitrate, step through its forms with Next form, then switch to Hybrid.

resonance.detailsHybridPattern: {{name}}, {{formula}}. Showing the hybrid: {{bonds}}. Average formal charges: {{charges}}.
resonance.detailsDrawPattern: {{name}}, {{formula}}. Drawing a resonance form on the skeleton. {{budget}} {{hint}}

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows the level choices or, during a round, the problem: a formula to draw on the board with the element palette.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has the score and level, the Hint, Check and Next buttons, and Reset All.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Choose a level, then draw each structure and press Check. Hints cost one point each.

challenge.levelButtonHelp: Starts a round of five problems.
challenge.detailsPattern: Level {{level}}, problem {{number}} of {{count}}, score {{score}}. Draw {{name}}, {{formula}}. Hints used: {{hints}}. {{state}}

preferences.title: Simulation
preferences.octetPolicy: Expanded octets (P, S, Cl and below)
preferences.acceptBoth: Accept both: smallest formal charges is best, octet answers also correct
preferences.octetFirst: Octet first: expand only when there is no other way
preferences.minimizeFormalCharge: Smallest formal charges, even when an octet expands
preferences.octetPolicyNote: Textbooks disagree on ions such as SO<sub>4</sub><sup>2−</sup>: OpenStax minimises formal charge (two S=O), while the octet view keeps four S–O bonds.

keyboardHelp.confirm: Make the bond, or drop the atom
keyboardHelp.grabAtom: Pick up the atom to move it

explanations.majorSingle: The only structure with the smallest formal charges. The other forms contribute little.
explanations.equivalentPattern: One of {{count}} equivalent forms: they differ only in where the electrons sit, so the real species is an average of all {{count}}, the hybrid.
explanations.alternative: Every atom keeps an octet, at the cost of larger formal charges. Textbooks that follow the octet rule draw this form.
explanations.acceptable: Formal charges as small as the best form, but the negative charge is on a less electronegative atom, so this form contributes less.
explanations.minor: Larger formal charges than the best form: a minor contributor.

resonance.hybridPattern: The hybrid averages the {{count}} equivalent forms: bonds that change between forms get the same fractional order, and the charge is shared.
resonance.hybridSingle: There is only one best form, so the hybrid is that structure.
resonance.noArrows: No electron pair moves between these forms.
resonance.lonePairToBondPattern: a lone pair on {{atom}} becomes a bond to {{other}}
resonance.bondToLonePairPattern: a pair from the {{a}}–{{b}} bond moves onto {{atom}}
resonance.drawHint: Add bonds and lone pairs to the skeleton, then press Check to see which resonance form you drew.
resonance.other: A valid structure, but not one of the forms shown: its formal charges are larger.
resonance.wrongSkeleton: Keep the skeleton: resonance forms move electrons, never atoms.
resonance.incomplete: Not finished yet: work through the checklist.

challenge.noHints: Stuck? Each hint costs one point; the fifth shows the answer.

hints.electronsPattern: Count the electrons: {{total}} valence electrons ({{fromAtoms}} from the atoms{{chargePart}}).
hints.centralPattern: {{element}} is the central atom: the least electronegative atom other than H.
hints.chain: There is no single central atom: the atoms form a chain or a ring. H always sits on the outside, with one bond.
hints.pair: With only two atoms, they are simply bonded to each other.
hints.skeleton: The skeleton is on the board: now add bonds and lone pairs.
hints.incompletePattern: {{element}} keeps only {{count}} electrons: it is stable with fewer than eight.
hints.radicalPattern: The odd electron stays unpaired on {{element}}.
hints.allSingle: Every bond is single: place the remaining electrons as lone pairs.
hints.answer: Here is the answer. Study it, then press Check to go on.

challenge.revealed: No points for this one, but now you know it.

shape.finishFirst: Finish the structure to see its shape.
shape.manyCenters: More than one central atom: the shape around each one is
